hook: A tank of ammonia gas at a fertilizer plant, a block of ice and a diamond ring all have a measured entropy, a number in a table. Those numbers let a chemist calculate the entropy change of a reaction before running it, the same way a table of enthalpies of formation gives ΔH°.

prereq.q: For which process does the entropy of the system increase?
options: Dry ice turning to CO₂ gas
prereq.why: Solid to gas disperses the matter; the others reduce the dispersal.

prereq.q: How is ΔH°rxn found from standard enthalpies of formation?
options: Σ ΔH°f(reactants) − Σ ΔH°f(products), without coefficients
Multiply all the ΔH°f values together
Add every ΔH°f value in the equation
prereq.why: Products minus reactants, each multiplied by its coefficient.

figure.caption: Standard molar entropies at 298 K: solids smallest, then liquids, then gases; among gases, bigger molecules have more.

chain.cause: A perfect crystal at 0 K has a single arrangement of its particles and energy
chain.effect: its entropy is zero, the starting point for measuring every S°

chain.cause: Any substance above 0 K has motion and so more than one microstate
chain.effect: the standard molar entropy S° of every pure substance at 298 K is positive, elements included

chain.cause: Entropy is a state function measured per mole
chain.effect: ΔS° of a reaction is Σ nS°(products) − Σ nS°(reactants)

chain.cause: The result should match the change in moles of gas
chain.effect: checking its sign catches missing coefficients and sign slips

ideas: A perfect crystal at 0 K has S = 0; every pure substance at 298 K has a positive S°, elements included (unlike ΔH°f).
S° values: gases ≫ liquids > solids; among similar substances, more atoms per molecule means a larger S°.
ΔS° = Σ nS°(products) − Σ nS°(reactants), each multiplied by its coefficient. Units: J/(mol·K).
Reverse a reaction: flip the sign. Double it: double ΔS°.
Check the sign of the answer against the change in moles of gas.

misconception.wrong: Elements in their standard states have S° = 0, just as they have ΔH°f = 0.
misconception.right: ΔH°f is zero for an element by definition. S° is measured from zero at 0 K, so every pure substance at 298 K, elements included, has a positive S°: O₂(g) has 205.2 J/(mol·K).

summary: Standard molar entropies S° are measured up from zero for a perfect crystal at 0 K, so every one is positive. The entropy change of a reaction is the sum of nS° for the products minus the sum for the reactants, in J/(mol·K). Its sign should agree with the change in moles of gas.
